title: A retro boarding pass scanner
summary: Drag the pass through a beige reader: too fast is an error, steady gets you in.
brief: Build a beige boarding pass scanner that reads a pass as I drag it through the slot. Reject a fast swipe with a red light and grant access on a steady swipe.

prompts.text:
Make an interactive vintage boarding pass scanner page with the original ATU AIR pass from our earlier recording: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heyatu/awesome-agent-showcase/b0c30bc4837baf2db322ba543070a315748d079c/entries/x-2098082543966867524/media/pass-scanner.mp4. Ask before downloading that MP4, installing anything or loading another resource. Use existing local tools: take only the printed ticket from the first unobstructed frame, undo its 2.8° clockwise tilt about (480,125), and crop a rounded 445 × 210 coupon. Keep its original print and stub. Never put the recording, recorded cursor or brand overlay on the page.
Centre a proportional 960 × 540 stage on pinkish ivory. The pass begins at x=257.5, y=20 and rolls 2.8° clockwise at rest. While held it follows the pointer with spring acceleration 220 × position error − 24 × velocity. Add roll −0.013° and yaw +0.034° per px/s of horizontal velocity and pitch −0.029° per px/s of vertical velocity, capped at ±11°, ±26°, ±18° respectively. Damp the angles at 13/s, perspective 620 px. Full spring and tilt up to docking: never reduce tilt with height or proximity. After 139 px downward movement over the slot, dock and ease towards zero angles, then constrain travel to the slot; on lift-out reinstate the full spring immediately. Keep the sheen tilt-driven and idle still.
The coupon goes BETWEEN two pieces of moulded beige plastic. Build the layers as siblings in one stacking context. At the back: a raised rounded rear rail at x=264, y=310, width 432, height 21, plus a narrow dark inner-shadowed channel just in front of it. Above that: the moving paper. In the foreground: the 445 px wide vented top and entire front body, beginning at y=332 and ending at y=456. Nothing enclosing both reader pieces may stack above the paper. A thin soft shadow from the front edge falls back onto the ticket at y=331. With the pass resting high, show the rear rail AND dark slot. While inserted the pass covers the rear rail; where the paper ends, the rear rail shows again. The front body hides the paper below the slot line only across its own width (paper overhanging the left edge can still show). At full insertion set the ticket top to y=201, leaving 131 of 210 px visible above the front edge at y=332. Make this layering clear when swiping left: a strip of rear rail shows on the right, paper in front of it, front lip in front of the paper.
Use the same state colour for BOTH the lens and the lit dots of the display: neutral grey for READY, amber READING, red ERROR, green SUCCESS. Do not hardcode amber text for all states. On the near top shelf show two banks of short vent slits, then a separate solid projecting beige lip. Give the lower face 84 px of height, broad bevels, soft highlights and a deep contact shadow. Inset two blank side pads and a central black 205 × 52 px glass display with small glowing 18–20 px dot-matrix letters. At the far right put a 9 px round lens in a dark bezel. READY is unlit; READING, ERROR and SUCCESS glow yellow, red and green, with a hot core and wide soft halo spilling across the plastic, saturated at radius 18 px and fading to zero at 42 px.
A fast 145 px sideways swipe in half a second gives ERROR; leave ERROR on release until the next action. A steady two-second swipe gives SUCCESS and changes “Swipe boarding pass to enter” to “Access granted”. Automatically after SUCCESS: hold 850 ms, release pointer capture and animate the actual ticket flying up and right off screen. Restore its exact starting position, tilt, caption, lamp and READY state without any more user input within 2 seconds. Verify fly-away and automatic reset in the browser after lifting your finger; do not substitute a manual lift-out for this ending. Build it in a new folder inside the current project folder with only local HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Open the result in the browser and check it. Ask me before installing or loading anything.

made.alt: A paper boarding pass tilts as the cursor changes direction, then straightens behind a beige scanner. The fast swipe shows ERROR. A steady swipe shows SUCCESS before the pass flies away and the reader resets.
made.caption: A fast swipe fails. A steady swipe turns the light green and grants access.
